column1: # markers.tsv — the marker greps from docs/reference/hermes-update-plan-v2026.8.3.md
# §Phase 4, turned into a machine-checkable list.
# Every row is a string that MUST be present in the built image's hermes tree.
# verify-markers.sh greps them all and fails the build if any is missing. This
# is the mechanism that catches, at build time and not on a live tenant:
#   * an upstream release that silently dropped a fix we rely on (the OAuth
#     billing lane — see docs/reference/hermes-400-extra-usage-fix.md); and
#   * a patch that "applied cleanly" into the wrong place after a refactor.
# Format: 4 TAB-separated columns.
#   id       short label used in build/CI output
#   file     path relative to the hermes install root (/opt/hermes)
#   pattern  fixed string (grep -F) that must appear in that file
#   required "required" -> missing is a build failure
#            "optional" -> missing is a warning (use for patches not yet
#                          vendored into this repo, so the image still builds)
# Do not use a regex here on purpose: fixed strings survive reformatting, and
# a marker that quietly stops matching because of an escaping subtlety is worse
# than no marker at all.
# id
# The OAuth wire-name promotion. If this disappears, Claude Max / subscription
# OAuth traffic flips from plan-billing to the extra-usage lane and tenants get
# HTTP 400 "out of extra usage". Update plan §1: "the self-update script's
# verification markers ... are both still valid".
upstream-oauth-wire-name
# The double-underscore MCP tool prefix constant that the promotion writes to.
# A single `mcp_` is the exact token that triggers the extra-usage lane.
upstream-mcp-prefix
# --- Patch target files must still exist ------------------------------------
# Cheap structural check: the update plan's file-disjoint patch rule assigns
# 001 -> anthropic_adapter.py, 002 -> approval.py, 003 -> slash_commands.py.
# If upstream moves or renames one of these, the corresponding patch will fail
# to apply — this row makes the reason obvious in the build log.
patch-002-target
patch-003-target
# These correspond to the founder's patches 001/002/003, which are NOT yet
# vendored into tenant-image/patches/ (they live on the VPS at
# ~/.hermes/patches/). They are marked `optional` so the image builds without
# them; flip each to `required` in the same commit that adds its .patch file.
# 001 — OAuth system-prompt scrubber. Marker per update plan §Phase 4:
#       `grep '/home/agent' agent/anthropic_adapter.py`
squire-001-oauth-scrubber
